summary.summary: Covering report presenting the draft Annual Governance Statement for 2025/26 (the AGS itself is Appendix 1, a separate document). Two points matter for a lender. First, the draft AGS has been published alongside the council's draft 2025/26 Statement of Accounts, with the final versions due by the 31 January 2027 statutory deadline after a further update in October 2026 — the reporting cycle is on its statutory track. Second, the council says no NEW significant governance issues have arisen since the final 2024/25 AGS was approved in February 2026, but the existing ones continue: the draft focuses on updating progress on financial sustainability, improvement and transformation, governance and internal control, leadership capacity, children's services improvement and partnership working. In short, a council still working through a known list of significant issues, with no fresh deterioration disclosed and no figures in this paper.

signals.headline: Draft AGS 2025/26 published alongside the draft 2025/26 Statement of Accounts, in line with statutory requirements; final accountability statements due by the 31 January 2027 backstop after an October 2026 committee update
signals.why: The unaudited 2025/26 balance sheet is now public and the governance disclosures around it are on the statutory timetable rather than slipping.

compliance.notes: High-quality, Arlingclose-advised strategy: strongest areas are the liability benchmark (charted to the end of the debt profile with all balances and assumptions), the full prudential-indicator suite, the capital strategy/MRP and a comprehensive investment strategy covering the council's ~£60m of service/commercial investments. Weakest areas are formal governance artefacts not restated in the annual documents (no explicit adoption of the TM Code's four clauses; no audit-qualification flag; no explicit sterling-only borrowing statement or paras 51-53 compliance statement; no formal IMPs), and, for a commercial investor, no quantified commercial/service-income dependence ratio. Note: the packet's capital_strategy.url (s134122) was a 2027/28 MTFS-assumptions Cabinet paper with no capital-strategy content; the real Capital/Investment strategies and prudential indicators were read from the MTFS 2026-2030 full report (Annexes 5, 6, B, C). The packet TMSS url (s131504) was a cover report; the real TMSS is Annex 7 (s131505).

news_drafts.headline: Cheshire East's 2026/27 forecast balances only with £24.995m of government-approved support; £15m gap set for 2027/28
news_drafts.lead:
Cheshire East Council expects to end 2026/27 with spending matching its budget, but only after applying £24.995m of exceptional financial support (EFS), permission from government to borrow or sell assets to cover day-to-day spending. The first-quarter budget forecast, before the Corporate Overview and Scrutiny Committee on 19 October, says this matches the amount assumed when the budget was set. Service budgets are forecast to underspend by £1.594m, offset by an equal overspend on central budgets.

The forecast also relies on £5.799m held back for transformation work and £15.358m of general contingency, of which £10.336m is for service pressures and £5.022m for central pressures. The council's chief finance officer says the balanced position also depends on delivering savings, containing demand-led spending, achieving capital receipts (money from asset sales) and managing higher financing costs. The 2026/27 budget included a reset of transformation savings.

The council's improvement and transformation delivery plan was rated Green on three of its four priorities at the end of June 2026. Financial sustainability was rated Amber, "at risk", because of the continued reliance on EFS. For 2027/28 the chief finance officer says "robust and deliverable proposals" are needed to close a £15m funding gap, with the aim of ending that reliance. A separate paper on the 2027/28 budget says stronger financial control and clearer recovery arrangements are now in place, but describes the position as "exceptionally fragile" and usable reserves as "materially below the risk-assessed level".
news_drafts.paper_title: Annex 4 for 2026/27 Budget – Quarter 1 Forecast Outturn

news_drafts.headline: Cheshire East audit committee asks for quarterly reports on delivery against ministers' expectations
news_drafts.lead:
Cheshire East Council's Audit and Governance Committee has asked for quarterly assurance reports on how the council is meeting the expectations set by ministers. The request is recorded in the committee's action log for its meeting on 15 October 2026. Reporting is to begin at the next appropriate meeting.

The log says the reports should focus on "material exceptions, changes in risk, delivery against ministerial expectations and evidence that improvement is embedded and sustained." They are also to include evidence of organisational and cultural change, among them staff survey results and measures of whether improvement has lasted.

The papers describe the council as subject to a Best Value Notice, a formal government notice about how the council runs its services and money. The action log gives no figures, dates for the notice, or details of what ministers have asked for.
news_drafts.paper_title: Audit and Governance Committee Action Log - October 2026

news_drafts.headline: Cheshire East balances 2026/27 forecast using £24.995m of exceptional financial support, about 5% of budget
news_drafts.lead:
Cheshire East Council has reached a balanced forecast for 2026/27 only through the planned use of £24.995m of exceptional financial support, according to a minute extract from its Cabinet considered in the papers for the full Council meeting on 14 October 2026. Exceptional financial support is government permission to borrow, or sell assets, to cover day-to-day spending, and is a last resort.

The sum is roughly 5% of the council's net service budget of around £450m. The minute says the balanced position was "achieved through the planned use of £24.995m of Exceptional Financial Support". The paper records that, despite the balanced forecast, Cabinet noted the continued fragility of the council's financial resilience.

The extract comes from the Cabinet's handling of supplementary revenue requests, which are requests for extra day-to-day spending authority during the year. The material before the desk does not set out which services the money supports, how the support will be financed, or what the council plans to do to reduce its reliance on it in later years.

findings.paper_title: Budget 2027/28 and MTFS 2027/31 UpdateCabinet and Committee Report Template
findings.headline: Four new Transformation Directors appointed to deliver improvement plan by end-November 2026 to identify further savings
findings.detail: The Council has completed recruitment of four Transformation Directors tasked with producing an integrated improvement and transformation delivery plan by end-November 2026. These directors will operate across all business areas. The plan outputs will inform the next MTFS update for Cabinet consideration in December 2026, where further savings options are expected to be presented.
findings.matters: Indicates the Council recognises the £10.6m remaining gap requires structured delivery capacity and dedicated leadership, signalling management intent to find further savings beyond those already identified.
findings.figures: Four new Transformation Directors; delivery plan due end-November 2026
findings.quote: the Council has recently completed a recruitment process to increase the number of Transformation Directors to support all areas of the Council's activities. Whilst these four Transformation Directors will support their specific business areas they have been tasked with the production of a single and holistic extension to the improvement and transformation delivery plan by the end of November 2026.

findings.paper_title: Budget 2027/28 and MTFS 2027/31 UpdateCabinet and Committee Report Template
findings.headline: Medium-term funding gaps remain substantial: £14.137m (2028/29) peaking at £19.827m (2029/30), reducing to £6.890m (2030/31) through Council Tax increases
findings.detail: Beyond 2027/28, the Council faces significant unfunded gaps across the entire medium-term forecast. The gap expands to £14.137m in 2028/29 and peaks at £19.827m in 2029/30, narrowing only to £6.890m in 2030/31. This improvement depends substantially on Council Tax assumptions rising from £348.974m in 2027/28 to £415.401m in 2030/31—an increase of £66.427m—which may face local political resistance.
findings.matters: Demonstrates a structural, multi-year financial challenge; the improvement in 2030/31 rests not on problem-solving but on substantial revenue growth outside the council's direct control and politically vulnerable.
findings.quote: Table 2 shows Exceptional Financial Support Funding Position (+shortfall) 10.619, 14.137, 19.827, 6.890; Council Tax (348.974), (369.859), (391.964), (415.401)

findings.paper_title: Budget 2027/28 and MTFS 2027/31 UpdateCabinet and Committee Report Template
findings.headline: Council requires Exceptional Financial Support to balance 2026/27-2030/31 budgets with usable reserves materially below risk-assessed levels
findings.detail: Despite stronger financial controls and clearer recovery arrangements, the Council continues to require Exceptional Financial Support (EFS) to balance its budget. Usable reserves are stated to be 'materially below the risk-assessed level'. The paper identifies demand-led pressures, savings delivery risks and balance-sheet challenges that 'leave limited capacity to absorb further financial shocks without corrective action or changes to the recovery plan'. The reliance on EFS is explicitly characterised as unsustainable medium to long term.
findings.matters: EFS is temporary emergency funding not available indefinitely; low reserves combined with demand and delivery risks leave minimal margin for error, making the council extremely vulnerable to unexpected costs or delays in savings realisation.
findings.figures: Reserves remain below risk-assessed levels; EFS required across entire 2026/27-2030/31 forecast period
findings.quote: The Council's financial position remains exceptionally fragile. Although stronger financial control and clearer recovery arrangements are now in place, the Council continues to rely on Exceptional Financial Support.

findings.paper_title: Budget 2027/28 and MTFS 2027/31 UpdateCabinet and Committee Report Template
findings.headline: £4.652m of budget savings identified and recognised for 2027/28, reducing gap from £15.271m to £10.619m
findings.detail: Following three joint Corporate Leadership Team and Cabinet Budget Control Workshops, the Council has formally recognised £4.652m of savings schemes that have been worked up to business case level and can be delivered in 2027/28. This reduces the original gap of £15.271m to £10.619m. Further budget ideas remain under scrutiny and will be reviewed ahead of the Cabinet meeting in December 2026. The Council must set a legal balanced budget by 11 March 2027.
findings.matters: Shows tangible progress on closing the gap but indicates the significant scale of remaining work, with nearly two-thirds of the original gap still unfunded and uncertain delivery ahead of the statutory deadline.
findings.figures: £4.652m savings recognised; gap reduced from £15.271m to £10.619m for 2027/28
findings.quote: Following three joint Corporate Leadership Team and Cabinet Budget Control Workshops the Council has been able to recognise savings of £4.652m within the 2027/28 Budget. This has reduced the approved MTFS financial gap of £15.271m to £10.619m.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Corporate Improvement and Transformation Delivery Plan - ACHIEVEMENTS UPDATED SEPT 26.docx
findings.headline: Prevent Reduce Enable pilot completed in Adults transformation programme, delivering ongoing savings and improved outcomes
findings.detail: The council completed the Prevent Reduce Enable pilot as part of its Adults transformation programme. Ongoing progress is being made to deliver both savings and better outcomes. This demonstrates that transformation activity in adult services is yielding financial benefits alongside service improvements.
findings.matters: Achieving savings while improving outcomes shows the council is capturing efficiency gains in its largest budget area; demonstrates transformation programmes can deliver financial benefit
findings.figures: Savings and improved outcomes in delivery (specific figures not quantified in paper)
findings.quote: Completed the Prevent Reduce Enable pilot which is part of the Adults transformation programme with ongoing progress being made to deliver both savings and better outcomes
